meta.title: Dress Right Clothing Corp. — Phase 2: Adjusting Entries
meta.description: July 31, 2027 period-end adjusting journal entries for Dress Right Clothing Corporation. Covers supplies used, expired rent, equipment depreciation, earned rent revenue, accrued salaries, and accrued interest.
learning_objectives: Record supplies used as an expense (asset-to-expense adjustment)
Record monthly depreciation on equipment (asset-to-expense adjustment)
Record earned portion of deferred revenue (liability-to-revenue adjustment)
Record accrued salaries at period-end (accrued expense adjustment)
Record accrued interest on notes payable (accrued expense adjustment)
Understand that AJEs NEVER involve the Cash account

transactions.description: Purchased $2,000 of supplies in July. Physical count on July 31 reveals $1,200 of supplies remain on hand. Supplies used = $2,000 − $1,200 = $800.
transactions.explanation: This is an asset-to-expense adjustment. Supplies (Asset) decreases → credit. Supplies Expense (Expense) increases → debit. The $800 of supplies consumed during July is recognized as an expense. The remaining $1,200 stays in the Supplies asset account for future periods.

transactions.description: Paid $24,000 on July 1 for 1 year rent. Monthly rent cost = $24,000 ÷ 12 = $2,000/month. One month expired in July.
transactions.explanation: This is an asset-to-expense adjustment. Prepaid Rent (Asset) decreases → credit. Rent Expense (Expense) increases → debit. One month of the prepaid rent has expired and is now recognized as an expense. The remaining $22,000 in Prepaid Rent covers 11 future months.

transactions.description: Office equipment cost $12,000 with a 5-year (60 months) useful life and zero residual value. Monthly straight-line depreciation = $12,000 ÷ 60 = $200/month.
transactions.explanation: This is an asset-to-expense adjustment using a contra-asset account. Depreciation Expense (Expense) increases → debit. Accumulated Depreciation (Contra-Asset) increases → credit. The contra-asset account reduces the book value of Office Equipment on the balance sheet without directly reducing the Equipment account.

transactions.description: Subleased space on July 16 for $500/month, collecting $1,000 advance for 2 months. By July 31, half of one month (0.5 month = $250) of service has been provided.
transactions.explanation: This is a liability-to-revenue adjustment. Deferred Rent Revenue (Liability) decreases → debit. Rent Revenue (Revenue) increases → credit. As the rental space is used, the liability is reduced and revenue is recognized. The remaining $750 in Deferred Rent Revenue represents 1.5 months of unearned rent.

transactions.description: Paid $5,000 on July 20 for the first half of July. Unpaid salaries earned by employees for the second half of July total $5,500 (to be paid in early August).
transactions.explanation: This is an accrued expense adjustment (liability-to-expense). Salaries Expense (Expense) increases → debit. Salaries Payable (Liability) increases → credit. The salaries earned by employees in the second half of July must be recognized as an expense in July even though payment will occur in August. Total July salaries = $5,000 (paid) + $5,500 (accrued) = $10,500.

transactions.description: Interest on the $40,000, 10% notes payable issued on July 1 for the month of July: Interest = $40,000 × 10% × 1/12 = $333 (rounded).
transactions.explanation: This is an accrued expense adjustment. Interest Expense (Expense) increases → debit. Interest Payable (Liability) increases → credit. The interest cost of borrowing $40,000 at 10% for one month must be recognized in July even though interest will be paid later (at note maturity).
